terms.gloss: as he (she) says: according to (him, her)
evidence: Gell. 1.18.2: nōn leporem dīcimus, ut ait
terms.comment: With the name: ut ait Ennius; with a book, ut scrībit; for hearsay, ut ajunt, as they say.

terms.gloss: X is the authority for it, X reports (with accusative and infinitive)
evidence: Tac. Ann. 13.20: Fabius Rūsticus auctor est (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: The historians’ way of naming a source; see source (of information).

phrases.latin: Graecia enim antīqua, ut scrībit Tīmaeus, taurōs vocābat italōs
phrases.english: for in ancient Greece, according to Timaeus, bulls were called italoi
we ought, as they say, to copy the bees

phrases.latin: tē in Ēpīrum salvum vēnisse et, ut scrībis, ex sententiā nāvigāsse vehementer gaudeō
phrases.english: I am delighted that you reached Epirus safely and, according to your letter, had the voyage you wanted

sources: Lewis & Short: aio · Lewis & Short: scribo · Lewis & Short: auctor
